ken: Starting bring-up for 'sundial-int6' (6-bit per-channel prototype) — running a quant sweep vs our conch-emb-512 fp16 baseline on wiki/product holdouts. Kicked off CI run: https://ci.internal/8120
maria: Cool. What's the run config (batch/seq/seed/holdout)?
ken: Run config in CI: batch=256, seq=128, seed=1234, holdout=wiki_holdout_50k.json. Tracked metrics: recall@1/10/100, silhouette, PCA variance, jaccard_top10, centroid drift.
sam: First pass finished — rough recall@10 drop ~4.1% relative to baseline on the 50k holdout.
ken: Raw from CI 8120: baseline recall@10=0.828, sundial-int6=0.794, recall@1 baseline=0.619, sundial=0.557.
maria: Yikes. Any pattern by query length or label?
ken: Short queries (<6 tokens) show the worst impact: recall@1 down ~7.0%. Medium (6-24) down ~3.5%. Long (>24) almost flat (~0.8% drop).
sam: Did you compare cosine vs dot? Quant can change vector norms and L2-norm distribution.
ken: Yes — we computed both. Dot-product reduces relative loss by ~0.4% but still a regression. Cosine delta ~ -4.0% vs baseline.
ken: Eval command used:
```
./tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model sundial-int6 \
  --baseline conch-emb-512-fp16 \
  --holdout /data/holdouts/wiki_holdout_50k.json \
  --metrics recall@1,recall@10,recall@100,silhouette,jaccard_topk,pca_var \
  --batch 256 --seed 1234
```
ci-bot: Job 8120 completed — FAILED (regression threshold exceeded). Tests triggered: recall_drop > 2%. :warning:
maria: Can you paste a few id-flip examples (query, baseline top1, sundial top1, sims)? Need qualitative sense.
ken: Pasting 4 representative short-query flips (trimmed):
1) Query: "install nginx" — baseline top1: doc#412 (apt install + config) sim=0.90, sundial top1: doc#990 (nginx modules) sim=0.63
2) Query: "refresh token oauth" — baseline top1: doc#1202 (refresh flow) sim=0.87, sundial: doc#3499 (jwt rotation) sim=0.59
3) Query: "merge branch conflict" — baseline top1: doc#57 (merge conflict resolution) sim=0.85, sundial: doc#411 (rebase gotchas) sim=0.65
4) Query: "python list comprehension" — baseline top1: doc#88 (examples) sim=0.92, sundial: doc#201 (map vs listcomp) sim=0.70
sam: Patterns suggest embeddings compress different subspaces; could be top-dim clipping or bias from per-channel scales.
maria: Agreed. Hypotheses: per-dim outliers getting clipped in quant, mis-scaled channels, or token-frequency-driven collapse. Try percentile clipping and a tiny affine calibration before quantization.
ken: Planned follow-ups: (A) per-channel symmetric int6 with 0.999 quantile clipping, (B) pre-quant affine scale (learned on 50k pairs), (C) light distillation (teacher=conch fp16, student=sundial-int6) on 200k pairs for 5k steps.
sam: Also compute Jaccard(top10) against baseline grouped by query-length buckets (<6, 6-24, >24) and per-label where available. That will quantify id-flips.
ken: Launching follow-up CI jobs: 8121 (perc-clip), 8122 (affine-calib), 8123 (distill-lite). Links: https://ci.internal/8121 https://ci.internal/8122 https://ci.internal/8123
maria: For distill, log recall vs steps and silhouette per coarse label — avoid overfitting to frequent labels. Also save 50 failure pairs per run.
ken: Will collect: per-length recall curves, Jaccard(top10) histograms, PCA variance explained (first 32 comps), and 10 sample id-flips. Estimated runtime ~2-3 hours for the 50k→200k runs.
ci-bot: Jobs queued: 8121 ETA 1h45m, 8122 ETA 2h, 8123 ETA 3h10m.
sam: If clipping + affine don't close the gap consider a hybrid quant scheme (rowwise high-precision for top-8 dims) or L2-normalize student before quant.
maria: Also check per-token embedding norm distributions pre/post quant. If mass shifts to small norms that's a red flag.
alex: @ken FYI I can bump GPU priority if distill needs it — ping me when 8123 hits prod queue.
ken: Thanks @alex — will ping if 8123 needs priority. Will post PCA plots and an aggregated metrics table when jobs finish. ETA ~3 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sam: Good plan. Tag me on the follow-up with the jaccard breakdown.
ken: Will do — will attach a tiny sample notebook to reproduce the problem locally as well. :memo:
